title: Freddie Jackson, romantic US singer with 10 R&B chart-toppers, dies aged 70
excerpt:
Celebrated for his earnest, dextrous voice, Jackson crossed into the pop charts with the hits Rock Me Tonight (For Old Times Sake) and You Are My Lady

Freddie Jackson, the US singer whose smooth and ...
body_text:
Celebrated for his earnest, dextrous voice, Jackson crossed into the pop charts with the hits Rock Me Tonight (For Old Times Sake) and You Are My Lady

Freddie Jackson, the US singer whose smooth and romantic take on R&B found a huge audience in the 1980s, has died aged 70.

A statement from his family on social media reads: “Freddie was more than a legendary voice. He was a kind, generous soul who loved his fans, his family, his friends and his music with everything he had. For decades he gave us the songs that became the soundtrack to our love stories, our celebrations and our most treasured memories. That gift will live on for ever.” No cause of death was given.

Blessed with a dextrous and technically brilliant voice that could flip from playful flirtation to earnest entreaties to crushed lamentations across the space of a single album, Jackson became a mainstay in the US R&B scene, earning 10 No 1 singles and four back to back No 1 albums on the country’s R&B charts. He also twice hit the main pop chart Top 20, with 1985’s Rock Me Tonight (For Old Times Sake) and You Are My Lady. The latter song also earned him two Grammy nominations.

Born in 1956, Jackson was raised in Harlem by a single mother, “eating collard greens and fried chicken”, he later said. “That’s not learned soul, it’s not acquired in some singing school or from copying what you hear on records. I live soul.”

He was first grounded in gospel music, performing at a local Baptist church, before expanding his musical remit outwards, establishing himself in New York’s music scene before moving to Los Angeles where he became the vocalist of dancefloor-focused soul group Mystic Merlin, recording their third album, Full Moon, with them.

After a spell as a backing singer for Melba Moore, eventually he was signed as a solo artist, modelling himself on “Black singers who were able to cross over to the pop market without selling out – Marvin Gaye, Sam Cooke, Al Green”. He released debut album Rock Me Tonight in 1985, which, containing the aforementioned hit singles, became a platinum seller and reached the US Top 10. Follow-up Just Like the First Time was also certified platinum, and four of its tracks – including a duet with Moore, A Little Bit More – hit R&B No 1.

His unabashed sensuality meant he was marketed with a “lover man” image, but he was careful not to let it define him. “I’m fortunate that a lot of ladies have liked the record and gone out and bought it,” he said. “But didn’t go to Capitol and say, ‘I’m a ladies man and I want to make a ladies man record.’ I don’t want to stereotype myself and my music. I don’t want to alienate anybody.”

Jackson was still topping at the R&B chart as late as 1991, but as the genre modernised and hip-hop emerged, Jackson’s style became less fashionable and his chart success waned. He nevertheless remained a familiar voice on R&B radio and continued to release new music, eventually putting out 15 studio albums.

In 2024, he announced he was living with kidney disease. “This journey has had its challenges but I’ve decided to face it with openness and resilience,” he said.

title: Ukraine accuses Russia of bombing apartment block as birthday gift for Putin
excerpt:
Building in Pryluky destroyed killing nine people including three children night before Russian president’s 74th birthday

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia’s military of deliberately killing civ...
body_text:
Building in Pryluky destroyed killing nine people including three children night before Russian president’s 74th birthday

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia’s military of deliberately killing civilians and bombing residential buildings as a macabre gift for Vladimir Putin, who celebrates his 74th birthday on Wednesday.

Ukraine’s president described Russia’s overnight drone and missiles strikes, which killed at least 15 people, as “despicable”. “The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively,” he said.

Video showed a ballistic missile slamming into a five-storey apartment block in the town of Pryluky in the northern Chernihiv region. The concrete building collapsed, entombing those inside. Nine people died, including three children, officials said, with 38 people injured.

Rescuers picked through the rubble in an attempt to find survivors. “Today, on Putin’s birthday, the Russian army ‘presented’ him with the destruction of a residential block in Pryluky. It was an ordinary five-storey block of flats,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media.

He acknowledged that Ukraine was struggling to shoot down enemy ballistic missiles, and appealed to allies to provide US-manufactured Patriot interceptors. “Air defence packages for us right now are a vital necessity,” he said.

The bombardment featured 70 ballistic missiles, as well as 46 jet-powered drones, which in recent weeks have been terrorising Ukrainians on a daily basis. Ukraine’s air force said it managed to down just over 80% of the fast-moving drones – an improvement on the previous average of 50% to 60%.

Eleven regions were hit. Two people were killed in Kyiv, with other deadly strikes in the central cities of Kremenchuk and Oleksandriia, where four civilians died. There was also extensive damage in Dnipro.

Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, said Russian generals had given Putin his favourite birthday present: “war crimes”. Moscow’s grim strategy of bombarding the country’s population so it capitulated would not work, he said.

“The Ukrainian people are not going to give up, because it’s about Ukraine’s survival as a nation and as a state,” he stated. The “ultimate” present would be a dock in The Hague, home to the international criminal court, where the Russian president would stand trial, Sybiha said.

One resident in Kremenchuk said the attack happened early on Wednesday. The woman told Ukrainian media: “We were making tea in the morning. My husband was getting ready for work. And that was it. I found myself on the floor. What can I say. It was very scary.”

Local people in Dnipro said a blast wave affected 16 buildings, blowing out doors and windows. One woman, Iryna, said her auto parts workshop had been hit for the sixth time. The ceiling collapsed in Wednesday’s strike, she said, with toilets, sinks and equipment damaged.

“The explosion happened around three in the morning. We were sleeping at home. Everyone was scared, probably the whole city heard it. We will restore the shop and continue to work,” she told the Suspline channel.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine had carried out its own long-range strikes on economic and military sites inside Russia. They included two oil complexes and a training ground in the ⁠Perm, ​Samara ‌and Astrakhan ‌regions.“These are ‌justified Ukrainian responses to ​all Russian attacks on ⁠our people,” ​he said.

The president posted dramatic video of a burning oil tanker close to the southern resort city of Sochi. Russian officials said naval drones had hit the Liberian-flagged ship, adding that “crude oil was burning openly on the Black Sea”. Its Indian crew of 23 was rescued, they said.

Both sides have heavily targeted commercial shipping around the Black Sea since Putin’s full-scale invasion in 2022. In recent weeks Russia has picked off vessels carrying Ukrainian grain, paralysing maritime traffic from Ukraine’s southern ports including Odesa.

Earlier this week, a civilian cargo ship sank after a suspected attack by Russian drones in the Black Sea. Its crew is still missing. A second vessel carrying grain was also hit while sailing in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, said the country’s prime minister, Rumen Radev. The search for survivors was called off on Wednesday, according to Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov of the Maritime Administration Executive ⁠Agency. “There are no ​traces of the sailors from the ‌first ship, and there will ‌be none,” he said.

title: Israeli attacks across Gaza kill at least four Palestinians
excerpt:

The Palestinian Civil Defence rescue volunteer was killed in an air strike a...
body_text:
Israeli attacks have killed at least four Palestinians, including a rescue worker, and wounded several others across Gaza.

The Palestinian Civil Defence rescue volunteer was killed in an air strike as he was travelling to help wounded people near Kamal Adwan Hospital in Beit Lahiya, northern Gaza, a medical source said on Wednesday.

The Civil Defence identified the victim as Mohamed Tamous.

Meanwhile, an Israeli drone strike in the southern city of Khan Younis killed Hisham Ibrahim Abu Mustafa, 60,  and injured several others, Nasser Hospital said.

The body of a 17-year-old Palestinian was also brought to Nasser Hospital after he was killed in an Israeli drone strike in the Qizan Abu Rashwan area south of Khan Younis, Turkiye’s state news agency Anadolu reported, citing a medical source.

A teenage boy died from wounds sustained last month when Israeli forces opened fire east of Khan Younis, Anadolu reported, citing a medical source.

Also on Wednesday, a girl was injured by Israeli gunfire directed at displaced Palestinians’ tents in the Al-Amal neighbourhood, Anadolu reported.

Additionally, in Khan Younis, the Israeli military carried out two demolitions in the northeastern and eastern parts of the city.

The military also carried out demolitions east of Gaza City’s Tuffah neighbourhood.

Israel has killed more than 74,245 Palestinians since it launched its genocidal war on Gaza in response to the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack on Israel.

The last thing we should do right now is rerun those arguments. Those were Andy Burnham’s exact words when he was campaigning in Makerfield.

(Interestingly, Badenoch does not address Burnham’s main claim, that Brexit has done “more harm than good”.

Badenoch says the country is running out of money.

But Labour is just proposing a “tax doom loop that is making us all poorer”, she says.

Badenoch says people think Conservatives are opposed to change. But that is wrong.

double quotation markThe world is constantly changing. New technologies, new challenges, new opportunities. It is only by adapting that we can preserve the very best of this country and hand something better onto the next generation. That is what being a Conservative means.

Andy Burnham says that we all just need to hope. Again. Hope is not a strategy. And since the last thing this country needs is a Paddington Bear prime minister hoping that the problems will just go away while Putin attacks our allies, while our economy flat lines.

Burnham wants to turn the clock back to the 1970s. Nostalgia is not a plan for our country.

Andy Burnham is promising a better yesterday. What I am promising is a better tomorrow.

Badenoch also attacks the Greens, saying the antisemitism at their conference was “disgraceful”. She goes on:

double quotation markThey are seeking to erase Jewish identity. Shame on the Green Party and shame on Zack Polanski.

Exactly three years ago today, we saw the horrific 7 October attacks, the worst slaughter of Jews since the Holocaust.

The Conservative party stands with the Jewish people. We will never stop fighting antisemitism.

Badenoch goes on to attack Reform UK over politicians like Suella Braveman suggesting that black people cannot be English. She says:

double quotation markI don’t want to live in a country run by people who threaten journalists, who call veterans ‘traitors’ and debate whether my mixed-race children are English.

I don’t want to explain to my son when I’m watching our brilliant England team play football that some people don’t think our black players are English.

I remember back in the day when Ian Wright and John Barnes were playing, nobody was questioning whether they were English. We certainly didn’t have sitting MPs questioning whether they were English.

We must not let these people take us backwards. That is not the country we are. Reform MPs are openly questioning people’s identity.

We are not like us, we are not like them, we are different, we are the Conservative party.

This gets one of the loudest rounds of applause of the speech so far.

Badenoch moves on to attack Reform UK. She says many Reform supporters are “our people”. But she attacks the party’s leadership.

double quotation markWe deserve better than Reform politicians. A year ago, those politicians were measuring up the curtains for No 10. Now, some of them are measuring up the curtains for their prison cells.

Let’s go through their greatest hits. Their leader in Wales was sent to prison for taking bribes from Russia. His successor then had to stand down after he was arrested last month. The police are investigating not just Robert Jenrick’s donations, but Richard Tice’s company as well.

Farage’s fishy £5m personal gift … The brown envelopes they boasted about on camera. Just when you think Reform couldn’t get any easier, there’s a convicted fraudster who calls himself ‘Posh George’ and calls Nigel Farage ‘daddy’.

double quotation markThe circus goes on and on and will never stop because this is who Reform politicians are. So to those who say ‘unite the right’, we are not uniting with that. People deserve better, they deserve better.

Badenoch criticises Burnham for wanting to have another debate on Brexit.

double quotation mark[Burnham] wants to reopen the Brexit debate. Can you imagine having to go through that again? So much time lost. Arguing with ourselves, arguing with the EU, going round and round in circles, businesses not knowing whether they should invest. He wants to do it all again. I think that is a terrible idea.

The last thing we should do right now is rerun those arguments. Those were Andy Burnham’s exact words when he was campaigning in Makerfield.

(Interestingly, Badenoch does not address Burnham’s main claim, that Brexit has done “more harm than good”.

double quotation markIn Liverpool last week, [Burnham] promised a National Care Service at a cost of £18 billion, without a plan to pay for it.

Yet again, we have a Labour prime minister making a promise that he cannot deliver, with sums that do not add up.

This is the wrong way of doing things. Fifty years ago the state was failing to run businesses. It had no business running British Leyland, British Telecom, British Airways, British Steel government – couldn’t manage them properly.

In fact, political interference made their problems worse.

Andy Burnham is wilfully ignorant of those lessons.

He doesn’t want to know because it doesn’t fit his worldview, so he is going to make the same mistakes and we will all pay for those mistakes.

Badenoch launches a sustained attack on Andy Burnham, accusing him of being unprincipled and opportunist.

double quotation markLabour are putting all their hope in just one man, but they don’t get a clean slate just because they have changed leader.

We are going to hold them to account and expose every single failure.

In fact, Andy Burnham doesn’t have a clean slate. This is a man he was happy to serve in Jeremy Corbyn’s shadow cabinet. He wasn’t the junior Defra PPS, he was the shadow home secretary, nodding along to a man who wanted to take the UK out of Nato, give up our nuclear deterrent and even disband our army.

When Andy Burnham was in opposition with Corbyn, he didn’t feel a need to change the leader.

But after Keir Starmer won a landslide, Burnham couldn’t wait to get back and take it off him.

That is who Andy Burnham is. Don’t let this man fool you with his fluttering eyelashes and his pork scratchings.

He said opening No 10 North was the best day of his life. Really? It’s got a fake cabinet room, a cardboard cut-out of Larry the Cat. And the address isn’t even number ten. It’s all make believe.

Badenoch claims the Tories are ready for an election.

double quotation markI want us to win in three years time.

To be honest. I want us to win next week.

We are ready for an election whenever it’s called, because we are the only party that understands what has gone wrong in Britain and knows how to put it right.

Badenoch says the Tories have changed – like M&S.

double quotation markWe have changed our party.

There is still a lot of work to do. People are looking through the shop window. They like what they see. But let’s be honest, not enough of them are buying it. We need to fix that.

A few weeks ago I was at London Fashion Week attending Marks and Spencer’s first ever catwalk show.

M&S is a brand that has been around for a hundred years. Not so long ago, critics said they were a bit stuffy and stuck in the past. Some were even questioning whether the brand would survive. Do you see where I’m going with this conference?

M&S is back in fashion. Great looks at affordable prices. They have adapted their style for today’s market and people are flooding back, including me.

And she urges people to stand for parliament as Conservatives.

double quotation markIf you’ve never thought about a career in politics, now’s your time.

Every single Conservative MP and candidate must bring Conservative values and principles to the table and stick to them.

So conference, all our candidates will sign a commitment to these high standards – integrity, duty, discipline. Common sense is non-negotiable.

The country needs to know that when you vote Conservative, you get Conservative.

Badenoch pays tribute to her shadow ministers.

double quotation markNo other party in Britain has got a team with talent like mine.

Repeating a joke Chris Philp made himself, she says this summer he was the first British politician to be fired on by the French navy since Trafalgar.

(Except they did not fire at him, and may not have known he was.)

Badenoch says the Tories have learned from their mistakes.

double quotation markUnlike Andy Burnham, I believe we need to learn from the past, not live in the past.

We have acknowledged our mistakes. We have set out what this party believes.

We are making it clear that those beliefs are expected of everyone who stands for us.

In the past, we had people who used our party to get elected and then betrayed our values.

I am building a united team of people, a team motivated by public service, not self-service.

And she says she has got rid of the trouble makers.

double quotation markThe plots and the infighting. Remember all that drama that’s gone?

The Conservatives have had an export boom. We have had an export boom of drama queens going to reform.

Badenoch accuses Andy Burnham of opening the door to a second independence referendum in Scotland.

(That is a reference to this Burnham answer at PMQs. Burnham later said he would not allow a second referendum.)

Badenoch says only the Conservatives will fight for the union.

title: Bar named in Cornell rape lawsuit disputes accuser's account, says she was never served alcohol while underage
excerpt: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas joins 'Fox & Friends' to report the latest on Cornell University's handling of a sexual assault investigation as students protest and call for resignations...
body_text:
Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas joins 'Fox & Friends' to report the latest on Cornell University's handling of a sexual assault investigation as students protest and call for resignations.

A bar named in the lawsuit at the center of the Cornell University sexual assault firestorm is disputing the alleged victim's claim that it served her alcohol while she was underage on the night of the alleged assault — a denial the bar has now also lodged in court.

Moonies Bar & Nightclub, a downtown Ithaca, New York bar popular with Cornell students, told Fox News that underage guests at a private Tri Delta sorority event on Oct. 19, 2024, were marked on their hands, while guests over 21 received wristbands. The bar says its bartenders served alcohol only to guests wearing wristbands.

The complaint and Moonies' account both say Doe was marked as underage. They differ over whether she was then served alcohol.

Doe's lawsuit alleges a Moonies bouncer placed an "X" on each of the then-20-year-old's hands to signify she was under 21, but that she was nevertheless served and consumed at least one alcoholic beverage inside the bar.

INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM

The Chi Phi fraternity house stands on the Cornell University campus in Ithaca, N.Y., on Oct. 2, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

"No alcohol was served to anyone who had mark on their hands," Moonies said in a statement to Fox News Tuesday, disputing the allegations.

CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS

Moonies also told Fox News that Doe later worked for the company from February to March 2025 and discussed the October 2024 incident during that period.

According to the bar, Doe never said during those conversations that she had been intoxicated at Moonies or served alcohol by one of its bartenders.

Fox News Digital contacted Doe's attorney for a response to both of Moonies' assertions.

In a formal answer filed Sunday in New York Supreme Court, Zareen Enterprises LLC, which does business as Moonies Bar & Nightclub, denied unlawfully selling or furnishing alcohol to anyone under the legal drinking age and denied selling or furnishing alcohol to any visibly intoxicated person.

The filing specifically denies the paragraph of Doe's complaint alleging she was served alcohol at Moonies despite having been marked as underage. Moonies also denied that any act or omission on its part caused Doe's alleged injuries.

The bar asked the court to dismiss the complaint against it in its entirety.

The dispute comes as the case has roiled Cornell and drawn national attention, with thousands rallying on campus Monday and faculty senators now pushing a no-confidence resolution against the university's central administration over its handling of sexual assault. Gov. Kathy Hochul has also appointed the New York Attorney General's Office as special prosecutor, with Attorney General Letitia James leading an "active criminal investigation."

Moonies said it hosted the private Tri Delta event from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m. that night with about 185 guests, including roughly 150 who were over 21 and 35 who were underage.

The bar said it had a contract with the sorority and marked underage guests' hands while providing wristbands to those over 21.

In the statement, Moonies called Doe's allegation that she was served alcohol "completely inaccurate," saying its employees "strictly followed the rules and did not serve alcohol to any underaged guests."

WATCH: CORNELL STUDENTS PROTEST SCHOOL'S HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT INVESTIGATION:

CORNELL PICKS FORMER DEPUTY US ATTORNEY GENERAL TO REVIEW SEX ASSAULT RESPONSE

In its court filing, Moonies also asserted as affirmative defenses that Doe cannot establish that it unlawfully sold alcohol to an underage or visibly intoxicated person, or that any alleged unlawful sale caused her injuries. The bar maintained that it complied with all applicable laws and regulations governing alcohol sales.

The dispute concerns one part of Doe's account of the hours preceding the alleged assault and what happened at Moonies before she arrived at Chi Phi.

According to her lawsuit, Doe began the evening drinking vodka at her Tri Delta sorority house before a sorority house mother accompanied her to Moonies. She later went to another Ithaca bar before leaving alone around 11 p.m. and walking to the Chi Phi fraternity house to meet a friend who was a member.

By the time she arrived at Chi Phi, Doe was visibly intoxicated and had consumed roughly 10 standard drinks over three hours, according to her complaint.

Once inside, Doe alleges she was given another beer before going upstairs, where two fraternity members pressured her into snorting what they said was ketamine, a drug she says she had never previously taken. She alleges they also gave her marijuana and high-proof liquor before sexual activity began.

Doe alleges other fraternity members became involved as the night progressed and that she eventually became "completely incapacitated." Seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers are accused in her lawsuit of sexual assault and rape.

Students protest on Ho Plaza at Cornell University, Monday October 5, 2026 in Ithaca, NY. in response to an The protest in response to an alleged sexual assault in 2024, accused are some members of the Chi Phi fraternity.  (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)

The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining that sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men.

The case burst into public view when Doe filed the 101-page lawsuit Sept. 16, nearly two years after the alleged encounter.

In addition to the seven former fraternity members, Doe sued Cornell University, Chi Phi and affiliated entities, her own Tri Delta sorority and Moonies, among others, alleging that institutions around her failed to protect her before, during and after the events of that night.

Students protest on Ho Plaza at Cornell University on Monday, Oct. 5, 2026, in Ithaca, N.Y., in response to an alleged sexual assault in 2024 involving members of the Chi Phi fraternity. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)

The lawsuit's allegations prompted renewed scrutiny of the original criminal investigation.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who initially declined to pursue charges, has said the six-page sworn statement his office received from Cornell University Police in 2024 did not allege that Doe was drugged against her will or gang-raped and instead described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual."

A fuller transcript of Doe's November 2024 police interviews later obtained by CBS New York included statements in which she distinguished the initial sexual encounter from later activity and explicitly told investigators she had been raped.

Van Houten said his office had never received that transcript.

Fox News' Michelle Langer contributed to this report.

Michael Dorgan is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business.

You can send tips to michael.dorgan@fox.com and follow him on Twitter @M_Dorgan.

title: Russia ‘pursuing strategy of terror’, EU’s von der Leyen says after deadly strikes on Ukraine – Europe live
excerpt:
Ukraine president confirms series of attacks on Pryluky, Dnipro, Kremenchik, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv

The European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen condemned the latest round of Russian attacks...
body_text:
Ukraine president confirms series of attacks on Pryluky, Dnipro, Kremenchik, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv

The European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen condemned the latest round of Russian attacks on Ukraine, blaming Moscow for “pursuing a deliberate strategy of terror.”

Announcing the commission’s move to disburse €1.24bn to Ukraine for drones and missiles, she said:

“Russia is pursuing a deliberate strategy of terror. Trying to make daily life impossible for Ukrainians who want to live in peace.

To protect people and infrastructure, Europe is stepping up. Others must step up their support too.”

Aftermath of Russian strikes on Ukraine – in pictures

Back to Ukraine, the death toll has gone up again, with another four people confirmed dead in Pryluky after a Russian missile hit a five-storey residential building.

The total death toll from today’s attacks is now at 19.

We are getting reports of a knife attack at a vocational school in Ostrołęka, Poland, which left at least seven people injured, including two seriously, as reported by Poland’s RMF FM radio.

The city mayor, Paweł Niewiadomski, confirmed in a statement that the situation has been contained.

French chemist Henri Kagan and Japanese chemist Kensō Soai have been awarded the 2026 Nobel prize in chemistry “for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.”

“Henri Kagan discovered a new way of manipulating chemical reactions, allowing a greater excess of one of the mirror images to be created than was previously assumed possible. His discovery has been revolutionary for chemists who develop reactions for the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, flavours, scents and new materials.

Kenso Soai designed the first chemical reaction in which only one of the potential mirror images was formed. Other than life itself, no one had ever achieved this feat. The Soai reaction is one of the most spectacular chemical experiments ever conducted.”

They are conducting a live experiment to explain all of that on the stream below, if you are into this sort of things.

In other news, the winner of the 2026 Nobel prize in chemistry is about to be announced.

The European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen condemned the latest round of Russian attacks on Ukraine, blaming Moscow for “pursuing a deliberate strategy of terror.”

Announcing the commission’s move to disburse €1.24bn to Ukraine for drones and missiles, she said:

“Russia is pursuing a deliberate strategy of terror. Trying to make daily life impossible for Ukrainians who want to live in peace.

To protect people and infrastructure, Europe is stepping up. Others must step up their support too.”

Back to Ukraine, the death toll from a Russian strike on an apartment building in Pryluky has gone up from five to nine.

It means that at least 15 people were killed in Russian attacks last night.

Meanwhile, US secretary of state Marco Rubio is in Greece this morning to discuss a range of bilateral issues, including on energy exports of US-produced liquified natural gas to parts of Europe.

Speaking alongside his Greek counterpart George ​Gerapetritis, Rubio said the two countries were “bound by a common heritage and by proud histories,” with “a long history of friendship and partnership,” calling it “a source of stability in an unstable world.”

He praised Greece’s decision to increase defence spending, and its role in fighting transnational criminal organisations, human trafficking and terrorism in the Mediterranean region.

“Greece is a true, strong and model Nato ally, a country that understands the importance of burden sharing and that is willing to work with partners to address critical threats to all member states,” he said.

But there are also some awkward questions that are likely to come up, with US media raising concerns about the US ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle’s conduct in closed talks with Greek officials. Rubio declined to comment on the issue.

Later today, Rubio is expected to deliver a major speech on democracy, calling for “a great renewal of the western spirit – an inheritance stretching from Athens and Rome to Christendom to the founding of the American Republic,” according to the state department’s briefing.

In another update, Zelenskyy said Ukraine carries out “just responses to all Russian strikes against our people,” with Ukrainian forces hitting two Russian oil facilities, among other targets.

“Over the past day, our warriors struck four targets that help Russia finance and wage its brutal war – two oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara, and Astrakhan regions. There was also a response in the Black Sea.”

Meanwhile, Bulgaria has halted its search for the missing crew of a ship that sank after being ⁠hit by a drone on Tuesday, Reuters reported.

As reported yesterday (Europe Live, Tuesday), two ships were hit in a drone attack in Bulgaria’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone. One sank and the other ⁠was damaged. The crew of the damaged ship were rescued, but the crew of the sunken one remain missing.

“There are no traces ​of the sailors from the first ‌ship, and there will be ‌none. There is also no information about drone remains,” he said on a Nova ‌TV morning show.

“A boat, three life rafts and parts of the ship’s equipment have been found.”

It was not immediately clear who carried out the attack involving air and sea drones in waters off the coastal town of Byala in eastern Bulgaria, but there are growing concerns about hybrid attacks by Russia as it wages war in ‌Ukraine.

Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched “one fo the most vile strikes” on Ukraine last night, targeting the country’s energy infrastructure overnight.

At least 11 people were killed, and more than 34 injured in a series of attacks on Pryluky, Dnipro, Kremenchik, Zaporizhzhia, and Kyiv, which Zelenskyy ironically called “a birthday gift for Putin” who turns 74 today.

“Russian ballistic missiles remain the greatest challenge. And air defense packages for us right now are a vital necessity. That is why every day we are looking for missiles for Patriot systems that can and must actually protect people’s lives here, in Ukrainian skies,” Zelenskyy said.

Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha went further, saying:

“On Putin’s birthday, Russian generals brought him his favorite present: war crimes.”

“What Russian generals fail to tell Putin is that he is not winning this war and never will. …

I urge all partners to give Putin real presents that will help him finally choose diplomacy over war. Stronger sanctions on his military-industrial complex, including facilities producing ballistic missiles and the Rassvet satellite system, as well as stronger support for Ukraine, including all kinds of air defence and energy assistance ahead of winter.

But his ultimate present will be a dock in The Hague. We are preparing the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression Against Ukraine for practical launch already next year. Putin and his friends should know that accountability is inevitable.”

Elsewhere, I will bring you the latest from France, as high school protests continue after a major march in Paris, which ended with sporadic vandalism and running skirmishes with riot police, and officers firing teargas and carrying out baton charges to disperse protesters.

Following allegations of police brutality, interior minister Laurent Nuñez suspended the use of stun grenades at the protests, after a 15-year-old reportedly lost a hand on Monday, and a 14-year old lost several teeth.

The French PM, Sébastien Lecornu, is expected to speak later today to set out his plans for responding to the protests.

I will bring you also all other news from across Europe.

It’s Wednesday, 7 October 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

title: Zelensky condemns 'vile' large-scale Russian attacks that killed 15
excerpt:
At least 15 people have died in overnight strikes across central and eastern Ukraine, in what Volodymyr Zelensky has described as one of Russia's "most vile" attacks.

Ukraine's president said a resid...
body_text:
At least 15 people have died in overnight strikes across central and eastern Ukraine, in what Volodymyr Zelensky has described as one of Russia's "most vile" attacks.

Ukraine's president said a residential building in Pryluky in the Chernihiv region was destroyed as a "birthday 'gift' to Putin", who turns 74 on Wednesday. Strikes also hit Kyiv,  Dnipro, Kremenchuk, Zaporizhzhia and Oleksandriya.

Zelensky said Ukraine had struck targets in attacks on Russia's Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions in the past 24 hours, adding there was "also a response in the Black Sea", without providing further details.

Moscow is yet to comment on the latest strikes.

"The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively," Zelensky said, adding that 70 missiles were fired in total.

In the social media post on Wednesday morning, Zelensky said five people had been killed and 26, including five children, injured in a strike on a five-storey apartment building in Pryluky.

He added that people could still be trapped in the rubble.

Chernihiv Oblast police later reported that the death toll had risen to nine after the bodies of three children were recovered, with emergency workers continuing a search operation.

Emergency workers were continuing to search for residents under the rubble of the apartment building in Pryluky on Wednesday morning

Two people were also killed and eight injured after Russian missile strikes damaged five apartment buildings in Dnipro and four high-rise buildings in Kremenchuk, said Zelensky.

Two people were also killed in the capital, Kyiv, and two others in Oleksandriya, he added.

Ukraine's national police posted pictures online showing what it says is an unexploded Russian Iskander missile in the middle of a Kyiv district. BBC Verify has confirmed the images are genuine and the apparent missile fragments came down in an area of open land surrounded by high-rise apartment buildings.

A video posted by the police shows people digging through collapsed remains of a residential building in Pryluky. Another verified video shows damage to cars and what appears to be rubble and a fallen tree in an area surrounded by apartment blocks in Kremenchuk.

A photograph of fragments of what police said was an unexploded Russian Iskander missile in Kyiv

Zelensky renewed a call for allies to provide air defence support packages to Ukraine, saying its military only managed to shoot down "some" of the missiles launched by Russia overnight.

According to Zelensky, one of the "key targets" of the attack was the country's energy infrastructure, which Moscow earlier said it would intensify strikes on following Ukraine's strikes on Moscow's energy facilities.

In a separate post on Wednesday, Zelensky said Ukraine had struck four targets in retaliatory attacks in the past 24 hours, including two oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions.

"There is also a response in the Black Sea," the Ukrainian president wrote.

On Tuesday evening, footage emerged showing a huge plume of smoke engulfing an oil tanker off the coast of Sochi, along the Black Sea in southern Russia.

The Russian transport ministry later said unmanned boats had attacked the Liberian-flagged Aframax Rio oil tanker. Authorities claim the crew was rescued.

Separately, Bulgaria has halted a search for the missing crew of a ship that sank after being hit by a drone on Tuesday, Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov from the Maritime Administration Executive Agency said, as reported by Bulgarian television network Nora TV.

Tracking data shows the ship was anchored at the southern end of the Bosphorus strait until Monday when it entered the Black Sea heading north. Its last reported position on ship-tracking site MarineTraffic was at 23:43 GMT on Monday in what is known as the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone of the Black Sea.

Bulgarian specialist news outlet Maritime.bg reported the Alfa Watan was attacked by a drone and sank 70nm (130km) east of Byala.

As well as the civilian cargo ship, a second vessel - carrying grain - was also hit within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, its Prime Minister Rumen Radev said on Tuesday. The 18 crew members on the second vessel were rescued.

Bulgaria has not said who it believes was behind the attacks.

It comes as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea, particularly the eastern side, as part of its war against Ukraine.

In an evening address on Tuesday, Zelensky claimed Russia was responsible for the attacks.

Moscow has not commented on the latest incident.

Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea

Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit

title: Trump’s LA and San Diego comments ‘dangerous, if not treasonous’, says Newsom – US politics live
excerpt:
California governor critcizes president for ‘putting a target on two of our biggest cities and one of America’s largest naval hubs’

California to ‘actively monitor’ possible threats after Trump said ...
body_text:
California governor critcizes president for ‘putting a target on two of our biggest cities and one of America’s largest naval hubs’

California to ‘actively monitor’ possible threats after Trump said Iran could ‘take out’ LA and San Diego

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Donald Trump was accused of “dangerous, if not treasonous” behaviour after his comments suggesting he could “let [Iran] take out” Los Angeles or San Diego.

California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, has since directed the state’s emergency preparedness center to “actively monitor” possible threats to the state.

“Donald Trump’s remarks were dangerous – if not treasonous – putting a target on two of our biggest cities and one of America’s largest naval hubs,” Newsom said in a post on X, adding that the state’s threat-assessment center would be on heightened alert “in the event that foreign actors interpret the president’s remarks as an invitation to target California”.

The president has faced a chorus of condemnation from Democratic leaders in California after his comments at a rally in Nebraska on Monday night, which the White House has suggested were being taken out of context.

At the president’s rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, Trump claimed that high prices due to the war with Iran are a “small price to pay for keeping the world safe – keeping our country safe”.

double quotation markThey can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego.

Xavier Becerra, the Democratic nominee for governor vying to succeed Newsom, said he wasn’t surprised by the president’s comments.

“Donald Trump is a known commodity – you know how he acts, you know how he behaves,” Becerra told reporters at a campaign event in Los Angeles on Tuesday. But he took a jab at Republicans who “profess that they should be the leaders of our state” but aren’t willing to “stand up to Donald Trump”.

Meanwhile, San Diego mayor Todd Gloria said in a statement that “the most fundamental responsibility of a president is to protect the American people - all of them.”

double quotation markNo American city, regardless of its politics or geography, should ever be described as expendable or an acceptable price to pay.

But the White House insisted that Trump was being willfully misinterpreted.

Steven Cheung, its director of communications, posted on X:

double quotation markThe media freakout over President Trump’s comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn’t been stopped. America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money.

But one Republican House candidate, Jim Desmond, who is running in a competitive San Diego-based seat, pushed back.

“America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our commander in chief is to protect the American people and our homeland,” Desmond, a former mayor of San Marcos, said in a statement.

The Cook Political Report has revised its predictions for the November midterm elections, saying “A Senate Majority is Squarely in Democrats’ Sights”. Cook amended its prediction for the Kansas Senate race from “Lean Republican” to “Toss Up” – a shocker for a state where no Democrat has won a Senate election since 1932.

Donald Trump announced a massive new shipyard, which will be funded by a combination of federal and private dollars, at Tradepoint Atlantic in Sparrows Point. Anduril Industries, which is owned by Trump’s friend and donor Palmer Luckey, plans to invest $3.7bn in the shipyard and the US Navy will contribute an additional $2.9bn.

The USS Lincoln will dock in San Diego tomorrow, completing a nearly year-long deployment that sparked controversy over living conditions aboard the aircraft carrier as it supported military operations in Iran. Defense secretary Pete Hegseth is expected to greet the crew when they arrive.

Trump ordered the FBI to investigate protesters in Los Angeles who were demonstrating against the president’s immigration crackdown, according to a whistleblower complaint that was submitted to the Senate judiciary committee. Jill Fields, a former supervisory intelligence analyst in the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, made the complaint following the federal response to anti-ICE demonstrations around the city’s federal buildings, and in residential area, early last year.

Most ⁠US voters think Donald Trump’s administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new regulations for the technology, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll.

The six-day survey, which ended on Monday, showed that wide swaths of the electorate see ⁠AI as a major threat to ⁠American jobs, underscoring growing skepticism of the technology ​from voters across the political spectrum.

The fast-advancing technology has become a matter of keen national interest amid reports of AI agents running amok and hacking into corporate computer networks, and warnings from prominent researchers that it could one day pose an existential threat to humanity.

Noisy, power-hungry ⁠data centers that power AI also increasingly pose a nuisance when they pop up near neighborhoods while jacking up utility bills.

Some 57% of registered voters in the poll – including a third of self-identified Republicans - said the Trump administration has not taken AI risks seriously enough or at all. Some 54% said the same about ⁠Congress.

Secretary of state Marco Rubio is set to call for the nations of the west to return to their civilizational roots and restore the values that drove the rise of Europe and North America to global dominance for centuries, AP reports.

In Athens to discuss deepening economic, energy and security cooperation with Greece, Rubio will deliver a speech later today overlooking the ruins of the Acropolis, a widely recognizable symbol of the city’s ancient civilization associated with the creation of popular participatory government and the social contract.

Rubio intends to remind listeners of qualities he says were born in Greece and later defined the West, such as curiosity, courage, ambition and a restless spirit of exploration and discovery of the unknown.

“It has become fashionable today to believe that enlightened foreign policy means prioritizing the ‘global community’ over one’s own people. Here, too, we have much more to learn from the men of Ancient Greece. They knew that there was nothing selfish or wrong about loyalty to your nation, nor in fighting to defend its interests above all else,” Rubio plans to say in the speech, excerpts of which were distributed by the state department.

“Today, we find ourselves at a crossroads,” he will say, according to the excerpts. “The next decade will write the story of the next century. The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world, or resigns itself to a future of atrophy, servitude, and decline. We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.”

Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced herself from Donald Trump in a televised debate with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson on Tuesday, as she sought to present an image of independence in a state that has voted against Trump three times.

Proclaiming herself as not the US president’s “favorite senator”, Collins made the highly unusual boast for a Republican that she had voted with Joe Biden, a Democrat, more than 90% of the time when he was president. She also emphasized her differences with her fellow Republicans, saying she voted against her own party more than any other senator.

Collins’ defensiveness came amid a determined onslaught from Jackson, 58, a veteran former state legislator who was getting his first chance to present himself to a broad audience since replacing Graham Platner as the Democratic candidate in a contest that could be vital to the party’s hopes of winning the Senate.

Platner, a former harbor master, was forced to withdraw from the race in July after facing sexual assault allegations, which he denied, leaving Democrats racing against the clock to replace a candidate who had built up momentum campaigning on a populist progressive platform.

Jackson painted Collins as a Trump loyalist, saying she voted with the president 96% of the time. He also doggedly focused on her 2018 vote for the conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh, tying it to the court’s subsequent overturning of Roe v Wade, which had for half a century guaranteed the national right to abortion.

“Tonight is about who you stand with when it matters,” Jackson said in a pithy opening statement. “Eight years ago today, Maine women went to DC and begged Senator Collins not to confirm Brett Kavanaugh, but she did it anyways.

“He helped overturn Roe v Wade, and today she says she has no regrets. Would you trust her to pick the next supreme court justice?”

California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, has since directed the state’s emergency preparedness center to “actively monitor” possible threats to the state.

Steven Cheung, its director of communications, posted on X:

title: Chinese military activity nearly doubles around key US ally in disputed waters
excerpt:
Footage captures the tense moment of impact between a Chinese Coast Guard ship and a Philippine fisheries vessel in the South China Sea. (Video one credit: Chinese Coast Guard)

China nearly doubled t...
body_text:
Footage captures the tense moment of impact between a Chinese Coast Guard ship and a Philippine fisheries vessel in the South China Sea. (Video one credit: Chinese Coast Guard)

China nearly doubled the number of military and coast guard ships it sent to a key flashpoint in the South China Sea last month, according to Manila's military.

It comes as a series of increasingly tense encounters raises the risk of confrontation with a U.S. treaty ally located in the disputed waters. The Armed Forces of the Philippines said it tracked 101 different Chinese navy and coast guard vessels around four disputed areas over the course of September, up from 56 in August and 48 in July.

The sharp increase comes as Chinese and Philippine forces have faced off both at sea and in the air, including an encounter over the weekend in which Manila accused a Chinese fighter jet of repeatedly maneuvering dangerously close to an unarmed Philippine patrol plane.

China claims sovereignty over most of the South China Sea, including waters that fall within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone, and uses coast guard ships, naval vessels and aircraft to assert those claims. Manila has continued patrolling the waters and resupplying Philippine positions, bringing forces from the two countries into repeated close contact.

A Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel, labeled DA-BFAR MMOV 3015, navigates in proximity to another ship during a maritime encounter. (Chinese Coast Guard)

US, CHINA STRIKE DEAL TO LOWER TARIFFS ON $30B IN GOODS AFTER TRUMP-XI WASHINGTON SUMMIT

The confrontations carry particular stakes for Washington: the Philippines is a U.S. treaty ally, and the U.S. has repeatedly said its Mutual Defense Treaty with Manila applies to armed attacks on Philippine armed forces, public vessels and aircraft — including in the South China Sea.

The latest Philippine count showed the largest number of Chinese vessels around Scarborough Shoal, where 39 different Chinese coast guard and People's Liberation Army Navy ships were observed during September.

Another 28 were tracked around Thitu Island, known in the Philippines as Pag-asa; 23 around Second Thomas Shoal; and 11 around Sabina Shoal.

Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad, an Armed Forces of the Philippines spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea, said the figures showed China's continued "illegal, coercive, aggressive and deceptive" activities in the region.

But Philippine officials stopped short of concluding that the jump represented a broader shift in China's strategy. Asked why the number had nearly doubled from August, Trinidad said the military wanted to examine a longer period before drawing conclusions about the trend.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, meets with U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Malacanang presidential palace in Manila, Philippines, Friday, March 28, 2025. (AP Photo/Basilio Sepe)

The increase comes as the two sides have repeatedly confronted each other around some of the same contested waters.

On Saturday, a Philippine C-208 maritime patrol aircraft was flying near Scarborough Shoal when it encountered two Chinese military aircraft, according to the Philippine military.

Manila said one of the aircraft, a Chinese J-16 fighter, repeatedly approached the unarmed Philippine plane and maneuvered in front of and behind it at what the military described as an unsafe distance.

"This incident is part of a recurring pattern of unsafe and coercive behavior against Philippine government vessels and aircraft conducting lawful operations," the Philippine military said.

The Philippine aircraft completed its mission and returned safely to base.

TRUMP ENVOY WARNS CHINA'S POWER MOVE AT SEA IS THREAT 'WE CANNOT AFFORD TO IGNORE'

Beijing offered a sharply different account, saying the Philippine aircraft had entered airspace over Huangyan Dao, China's name for Scarborough Shoal, without permission and that Chinese forces took "necessary measures" in response.

Scarborough Shoal sits about 120 miles west of the Philippine island of Luzon and has become one of the most persistent flashpoints between Beijing and Manila. China has effectively controlled access to the shoal since a 2012 standoff, while the Philippines maintains that it falls within its exclusive economic zone.

China claims sovereignty over Scarborough and much of the South China Sea, overlapping claims by the Philippines and several other Southeast Asian nations. An international tribunal ruled in 2016 that China's sweeping historic-rights claims in the South China Sea had no legal basis, a ruling Beijing rejects.

Two Philippine Coast Guard ships were reportedly surrounded by Chinese vessels in a tense standoff in the South China Sea on Monday, further raising tensions between the two countries, in the South China Sea, off the Philippines on March 24, 2025. (Philippine Coast Guard (PCG)/Anadolu via Getty Images)

The encounters have continued despite a recent diplomatic thaw between Washington and Beijing, with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping emphasizing stability in the relationship during Xi's state visit to Washington.

Days before the latest air encounter, Chinese coast guard and naval vessels moved to block a Philippine resupply mission to Second Thomas Shoal, another major flashpoint in the dispute.

The Philippines deliberately grounded the aging BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas in 1999 and keeps a small contingent of troops aboard the rusting ship to maintain its presence. Chinese vessels have repeatedly tried to block missions carrying food, water and other supplies to those troops.

The latest incidents put renewed attention on Washington's defense commitment to Manila. The two countries have been bound by their Mutual Defense Treaty since 1951, and the U.S. has said an armed attack on Philippine armed forces, aircraft or public vessels anywhere in the South China Sea would invoke U.S. obligations under the treaty.

title: Michael Douglas reveals he made five phone calls to five women the day he chose Catherine Zeta-Jones
excerpt:
Michael Douglas discusses surviving stage 4 cancer, maintaining a lasting marriage and his close relationship with son Cameron. The Oscar winner has written a new memoir, "One Helluva Ride."

Michael ...
body_text:
Michael Douglas discusses surviving stage 4 cancer, maintaining a lasting marriage and his close relationship with son Cameron. The Oscar winner has written a new memoir, "One Helluva Ride."

Michael Douglas didn’t just choose Catherine Zeta-Jones — he called five other women in one day to make sure she was the only one.

The two-time Oscar winner pulls back the curtain on his extraordinary life in his new memoir, "One Helluva Ride," revealing his struggle to escape his father Kirk Douglas’ towering shadow, his past affairs and drug use, his terrifying battle with stage IV cancer — and the highs and lows of his decades-long love story with the actress.

Douglas first fell head over heels for Zeta-Jones when she caught his eye in the 1998 movie "The Mask of Zorro." Douglas, who is 25 years older than Zeta-Jones, later came across an interview in which she said she liked older men. He thought he had a chance.

MICHAEL DOUGLAS CONFIRMS SECRET AFFAIR WITH KATHLEEN TURNER ON 'ROMANCING THE STONE' SET

Catherine Zeta-Jones and Michael Douglas attend the launch of the new Aston Martin DB12 at the Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc in Antibes on May 24, 2023, in Cannes, France. In his memoir, "One Helluva Ride," Douglas revealed that he broke up with five women before embarking on a romance with Zeta-Jones. (David M. Benett)

Douglas went on to meet Zeta-Jones at the Deauville Film Festival in France. As the evening came to an end, Douglas blurted out, "I'm going to be the father of your children."

Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.

"One Helluva Ride" by Michael Douglas is available now. (Grand Central Publishing)

Zeta-Jones wasn't exactly swept off her feet. She knew about Douglas’ reputation as a Hollywood womanizer and remained wary of his intentions. Douglas, however, was determined to convince her that this time he was serious.

Eventually, Zeta-Jones was willing to give Douglas a chance, but under one condition: he needed to be monogamous.

WATCH: MICHAEL DOUGLAS SHARES LESSONS ON CANCER, MARRIAGE AND FAMILY

"I'm not interested in dating you if you're dating other people," she told him. "You can either continue with them or end it and be with me."

That day, Douglas wrote, he made five phone calls to five women he was seeing who lived in different cities.

Catherine Zeta-Jones attends a photocall for Martin Campbell's movie "The Legend of Zorro" on Oct. 3, 2005, in Paris. "The Mask of Zorro" was released in 1998. (Getty Images)

"Just after my marriage, I had been seeing five other women," he wrote. "They knew I was recently separated and in the process of getting a divorce. I made sure they all lived in different cities, which felt like a respectful way to be nonmonogamous. None of them asked for a commitment or even asked what else I was up to. I am sure they were seeing other people, too."

Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones during the F1 Grand Prix of Las Vegas at Las Vegas Strip Circuit on Nov. 21, 2025, in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images)

He told each woman he had met someone and could no longer see her. According to Douglas, "they all took it well."

The couple married in 2000. They welcomed their son, Dylan, that year, followed by their daughter, Carys, in 2003. Today, the couple split their time between New York, Mallorca and Santa Barbara.

Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta Jones visit Children's Hospital for Wales in Cardiff, Wales, on June 20, 2006. (WireImage)

But their Hollywood love story hasn’t always been picture-perfect.

Carys Zeta Douglas, Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones attend the "Jeanne du Barry" screening and opening ceremony red carpet at the 76th annual Cannes Film Festival at Palais des Festivals in Cannes, France, on May 16, 2023. (WireImage)

In the book, Douglas wrote that in 2013, the couple went on vacation and, upon returning, "had a heart-to-heart" about their relationship.

Catherine Zeta-Jones and Michael Douglas attend the 2019 Netflix Primetime Emmy Awards after-party at Milk Studios in Los Angeles, on Sept. 22, 2019. (Getty Images for Netflix)

"We had been married for more than a decade," Douglas recalled. "We had just gone through a period where a number of challenges came at us all at once. We decided to take some time apart. We still loved each other immensely, but we needed to make sure that being married was the right thing for all of us."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Michael Douglas and Diandra Luker finalized their divorce in 2000, after which he married Catherine Zeta-Jones. (Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images)

"The entire ordeal was incredibly difficult," Douglas wrote. "Catherine and I have a very intense, deep love for each other. And we love our kids dearly. We worked hard to make sure they understood that this wasn't their fault. It wasn't anyone's fault. I had learned the hard way that staying together for the children isn't always the right course of action. Sometimes you need to take a step back and make sure you're doing what's best for your whole family."

Douglas and Zeta-Jones had weathered an extraordinarily difficult stretch for their family.

Michael Douglas is seen here sitting down for his first exclusive television interview since his cancer treatments. Douglas announced his stage IV cancer diagnosis on Aug. 16, 2010, and he has been in remission and cancer-free since January 2011. (NBC Newswire/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

In 2010, Douglas was diagnosed with cancer. That same year, his eldest son, Cameron Douglas, was battling addiction and was sentenced to five years in prison after pleading guilty to drug charges. At the same time, Douglas was embroiled in a legal dispute with his ex-wife, Diandra Luker, over proceeds from "Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps."

Michael Douglas and Diandra Luker were married for 23 years, from 1977 until their divorce was finalized in 2000. (Sygma via Getty Images)

In his memoir, Douglas acknowledged that the mounting pressure took a toll on his wife, writing that "all of that stress" was "heaped onto" Zeta-Jones.

Zeta-Jones and the couple’s two children, Dylan and Carys, stayed in the family’s home in Bedford, New York. Douglas rented another place nearby so he could still see the children. He and Zeta-Jones "spoke regularly, but not every day."

From left: Catherine Zeta-Jones, Michael Douglas and Carys Zeta Douglas attend the "Jeanne du Barry" screening and opening ceremony red carpet at the 76th annual Cannes Film Festival at Palais des Festivals on May 16, 2023, in Cannes, France. (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)

"Part of taking a break is actually taking a break, something Diandra and I had struggled to do productively," he wrote of his past marriage.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

From left: Dylan Michael Douglas, Michael Douglas and Cameron Douglas attend the Princess Grace Awards at The Pierre Hotel in New York City on Oct. 23, 2024. (Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)

"It was hard on the kids, and they were so strong during the entire ordeal," Douglas wrote. "They knew that we both loved them more than anything, and their trust in us never wavered."

As Douglas navigated the separation, he wrote that he never gave up hope that he and Zeta-Jones would reconcile.

Catherine Zeta-Jones and Michael Douglas attend the 17th Annual Night of Stars on Oct. 24, 2000, in New York City. The couple married Nov. 18, 2000, at New York's Plaza Hotel. (Getty Images)

"I love Catherine in a way that I have never loved any other woman," he wrote. "She's my wife, my best friend, and my life partner. I could never lose her."

Best supporting actress winner Catherine Zeta-Jones in the press room at the 75th Annual Academy Awards. She was pregnant with her daughter, Carys. (Joe Llano/WireImage)

"As Catherine and I were seeing each other more surrounding the kids — school functions, drop-offs, extracurricular activities — we realized we both missed each other enormously," he wrote. "Taking time away helped reignite the spark that had brought us together."

Catherine Zeta-Jones and Michael Douglas attend the "Entrapment" premiere at the Odeon cinema in Edinburgh, Scotland, on June 30, 1999. (Mirrorpix via Getty Images)

"Thank God we found our way back to each other," Douglas wrote. "Our marriage deserved a second chance. Today, our marriage is stronger than ever, and we recently celebrated our 25th wedding anniversary. We still love spending time together. We can play 18 holes or walk on the beach, or we can just sit on the couch all day long talking. After all these years, wherever we are in the world, Catherine Zeta-Jones is still an incredible date."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Catherine Zeta Jones and Michael Douglas stand on the second hole of The Old Course before the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship 2025 in St. Andrews, Scotland, on Sept. 30, 2025. (Getty Images)

After decades together, Douglas told Fox News Digital he has learned a major lesson about making a marriage last in Hollywood.

"Making that person, that partner, as special as 25 years later," he said. "Make her feel as special 25 years later as the first day you started wooing her. What happens sometimes, after a while, is compatibility, and we end up making more of an effort with strangers than the person closest to you. So, I think it really calls for mutual respect and a good sense of humor."

Michael Douglas attends the Women In Cinema event during the Red Sea International Film Festival 2024 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on Dec. 6, 2024. (Getty Images)

When asked what Zeta-Jones, 57, does that still makes him feel like the luckiest guy in the world, he didn't miss a beat.

Catherine Zeta-Jones and Michael Douglas attend the "Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania" UK gala screening at BFI IMAX Waterloo in London, England, on Feb. 16, 2023. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"Walk into a room," he said with a smile.

Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Former Australian bishop jailed for sexually abusing young men
excerpt:
Christopher Saunders, pictured in 2008, has been jailed for sexual offences against two young men

Former Australian bishop Christopher Saunders has been jailed for sexually abusing two young Aborigin...
body_text:
Christopher Saunders, pictured in 2008, has been jailed for sexual offences against two young men

Former Australian bishop Christopher Saunders has been jailed for sexually abusing two young Aboriginal men during his time as a Catholic cleric.

Saunders - who resigned as Bishop of Broome when first accused of wrongdoing in 2020 - was found guilty of one charge of rape and 12 counts of indecent assault in August.

The 76-year-old was on Wednesday sentenced to six and a half years in prison, but will be eligible for release on parole in February 2031.

He is one of the most senior Catholic leaders in the world to face sex abuse charges.

His trial in the state of Western Australia heard Saunders systematically groomed the two young men, inviting them to "shirts-off" gatherings and plying them with alcohol, often using church funds and church-owned properties to do so.

He was convicted of kissing and molesting the men between 2010 and 2019, and in one instance forcing oral sex on one of them.

Saunders was acquitted by the jury of alleged offences against a third young man.

In a victim impact statement provided to the court, that young man said he struggled to talk about what had happened.

"I was a toy that he was using,"  the victim said. "My head is pounding now, I'm in so much pain."

First ordained in 1976, Saunders spent most of his career in the remote Kimberley region in the nation's north-west corner, and was appointed Bishop of Broome in 1996.

The diocese stretches about 770,000 sq km (297,000 sq miles) - an area roughly the size of Turkey - and encompasses some of the most remote parts of the country.

District Court Judge Martin Flynn said Saunders had "disregarded the dignity" of his victims and caused them lasting harm.

In a statement, Archbishop of Perth Timothy Costelloe said the men who had come forward had shown great courage and resilience in pursuing justice.

"We are sorry for the pain and suffering that was inflicted on you. We are sorry that your trust was so directly and profoundly betrayed by a leader of the church," he said.

"No court sentence can undo the suffering that has been caused or restore all that each person has lost."

The accusations were first aired in 2020, but the initial police investigation that followed was closed without charge.

However after a historic inquiry was ordered by the Pope, police began a new investigation.

Costelloe has previously said the church's investigation into Saunders - paused when police resumed theirs - will restart.

The church is under pressure to strip Saunders of his remaining title and ministry powers, a decision the Archbishop said would be determined by Rome.

Only a handful of "Vos Estis Lux Mundi" - meaning "You Are the Light of the World" in Latin - inquiries have been undertaken around the world.

The investigations are commissioned by the pontiff and were introduced in 2019 to combat sexual abuse and hold bishops and other high-ranking Catholic Church officials accountable for their actions.

title: EU negotiators head to China hoping to curb cheap imports of hybrid electric cars
excerpt:
Mood in trade talks said to have changed as EU member states harden demands for protection against Chinese imports

EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at seal...
body_text:
Mood in trade talks said to have changed as EU member states harden demands for protection against Chinese imports

EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at sealing a breakthrough deal tackling Beijing’s record £1bn-a-day trade surplus by curbing its exports of cheap hybrid electric cars into Europe.

Trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and his team fly out on Wednesday and will be negotiating up to the wire in talks scheduled to start the following day and continue late into Friday.

Sources say they hope to achieve “tangible, meaningful and measurable” results before the meeting of EU leaders in Brussels on Thursday next week, where China is high on the agenda.

The main focus is on what has been described as a “proof of concept” pilot agreement involving one sector, which is expected to be cars, which could be scaled up for other sectors in the coming months.

Diplomatic efforts to avert a full-scale trade war started at the end of June, albeit with little hope that China could curb exports to the EU given its historic ability to pivot quickly any time trade barriers are put in its path. For example, after the EU imposed tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles in October 2024 there was a boom in exports of hybrid cars, which were not subject to tariffs.

Last month, the EU asked China to voluntarily restrict hybrid exports to address soaring sales, warning that if they did not restrict them, safeguards – which could include quotas – could be enacted.

It is not known what China’s response was. But sources say the mood in talks has changed as EU member states have hardened demands for protection against Chinese imports that threaten their own industries.

On Monday, Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, agreed a “historic U-turn” on its policy on China by siding with the French president, Emmanuel Macron, in authorising effective permission for EU leaders to approve a new instrument to allow them to defend trade by cutting access to the single market at short notice.

In a joint paper with Emmanuel Macron, the two countries spoke of “a massive industrial shock … affecting sectors at the heart of the European industrial model and of systemic relevance [pharmaceuticals, aerospace, automotive, machine tools, chemicals, etc.]”.

The paper called for the use of all existing trade defence tools, but also for a new diversification instrument and “possible additional” new measures to allow the bloc to react when “third countries seek to undermine the restoration of a level playing field”.

Andrew Small, a former EU adviser on China, said Šefčovič’s talks will test the resolve of both Beijing and Brussels and will “determine whether China is willing to put sufficiently serious offers on the table”.

Small, who is the Asia director at the European Council on Foreign Relations in Berlin, warned: “China’s most effective tactic may be to draw Europe into a ‘process trap’ offering just enough to delay action, without addressing the forces driving European deindustrialisation.”

Sources say the Franco-German proposals for a new instrument, dubbed a “kill switch”, were born out of frustration, particularly in Paris, that a so-called “trade bazooka” available to Brussels, officially known as the anti-coercion instrument, has never been used.

Paris pushed for the use of the ACI following Trump’s threat of tariffs last year but it never gained traction from others as it could take up to a year to implement.

Handlesblatt, the Germany business newspaper, described Monday’s change in policy as “nothing less than an economic turning point”, with chief political reporter Martin Greive concluding in a hard-hitting column that Merz was “putting an end to years of naiveté towards Beijing”.

“Merz has recognised in recent months that Germany is the epicentre of the China shock 2.0; that there might not be much left of German industry if Germany continues to stand by and watch as China gains enormous export advantages through trillions in subsidies, the unilateral siphoning off of knowhow, and a – to put it mildly – questionable monetary policy,” he wrote.

title: Former German spy chief arrested on suspicion of espionage, attempted treason
excerpt:

body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A former spy chief for Germany's foreign intelligence service was arrested Tuesday on suspicion of espionage and attempted treason over allegations that he obtained classified documents and used secret information to prepare an analysis for an employee of a foreign intelligence service, prosecutors said.

August Hanning, 80, led Germany's Federal Intelligence Service, known as the BND, from 1998 to 2005.

According to federal prosecutors, Hanning is "strongly suspected of treasonous espionage, spying out state secrets, attempted treason, and espionage."

A former aide, identified as Manfred D., was also arrested in western Germany and is accused of aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage in connection with the case.

RUNAWAY BRAZILIAN EX-SPY CHIEF CONVICTED IN COUP REPORTEDLY DETAINED BY ICE AT FLORIDA TRAFFIC STOP

August Hanning, the former head of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service, was arrested on suspicion of espionage and attempted treason, federal prosecutors said. (Michael Kappeler/dpa via AP)

Prosecutors said Manfred D. worked as Hanning’s chief of staff before going on to serve as chief of staff to several of Hanning's successors at the BND between March 2012 and March 2026, giving him access to confidential information.

Beginning in 2010, the men allegedly reached an agreement under which Manfred D. would routinely transmit intelligence to Hanning in exchange for payment.

The arrangement continued until June 2022, with Manfred D. allegedly providing Hanning with roughly 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information intended strictly for internal use, according to prosecutors.

Hanning allegedly used the information in his private consulting work.

US COUNTERINTELLIGENCE ‘WAY BEHIND,’ POST-9/11 RECORD ‘EXTRAORDINARILY NEGLIGENT’, FMR TRUMP WH OFFICIAL WARNS

Police officers are standing in front of the home of former president of the Federal Intelligence Service, or BND, August Hanning, 80, who was arrested on suspicion of espionage, in Nordwalde, Germany, Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (Christoph Reichwein/dpa via AP)

A spokesperson for the federal prosecutor’s office told German broadcaster RTL that investigators believe Hanning used classified information to prepare an analysis for an employee of a foreign intelligence service.

Prosecutors also said Hanning passed along information following extensive exchanges with an employee of another intelligence service.

German authorities have not publicly identified the foreign intelligence services allegedly involved.

The investigation grew out of an apparently unrelated case involving the 2024 abduction of the children of Hamburg businesswoman Christina Block during a custody dispute.

Prosecutors said Hanning's arrest stemmed from evidence gathered during that investigation.

CALIFORNIA REALTOR NABBED AT LAX IN ALLEGED CHINA SPY CASE TARGETING TAIWAN PRESIDENT’S RELATIVE

August Hanning led Germany's Federal Intelligence Service, known as the BND, from 1998 to 2005 before later working as a private consultant. (Michael Kappeler/dpa via AP)

Hanning's arrest marks the first detention of a former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, according to Reuters.

Hanning and Manfred D. were expected to appear before a judge at Germany's Federal Court of Justice following their arrests.

Fox News Digital has reached out to GLOBSEC, where Hanning previously held an affiliation, for comment on his arrest and the allegations against him.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
